transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Um, yeah—so, what brought me in is mostly work. I keep, like, leaving my station when I’m supposed to stay there, or I’ll just pop up in meetings when everybody’s sitting down, and I don’t even really notice until someone says something.

My supervisor said it’s turning into a safety issue, because I’ll kind of take off before I think it through. And I mean, I don’t want to get in trouble or anything—I need the job—but it’s like my body moves before my brain catches up.
Can you tell me if you noticed similar restlessness, trouble staying seated, or acting before thinking back when you were a child, say before age 12?

Yeah, definitely. Like, even in elementary school I was that kid who just could not stay in my seat. I’d get up and wander around the room, or start talking while the teacher was talking—just blurting stuff out before I even realized I did it.

My mom used to get notes sent home about it, and I remember being mad because I didn’t feel like I was trying to be bad. I’d just… do it. Like if something popped in my head, it came out, or if I wanted to go look at something, I was already across the room.
Do you often have trouble focusing on tasks, following through on instructions, or find yourself easily distracted and forgetful in daily activities?

Yeah… focusing is hard, especially if it’s something like inventory logs or those CNC training pages. I’ll start out really trying, like, “Okay, I’m gonna read this and get it done,” but after a few minutes the numbers or the words kind of blur together.

And then I realize I’ve been looking at the same section but didn’t actually take any of it in, so I have to go back over it again. Which is frustrating, because it’s not like I’m not trying. It just… doesn’t stick.
Do you notice this same kind of restlessness and trouble focusing happening outside of work too, like at home or when you're with friends or family?

Um… I don’t know, honestly. I mean, I guess I don’t really track it the same way at home because nobody’s, like, writing me up there, you know?

With friends it’s kind of different because we’re usually doing stuff, or talking, and then I’ll start telling one story and it reminds me of another thing—like the other day my cousin was talking about her car and then I remembered this whole thing about my neighbor’s truck being towed, which isn’t really what you asked.

So… yeah, I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I notice it more at work because it causes problems there.

Can you think of a specific recent example at home—like forgetting to finish a chore, interrupting a family member, or losing track of something you were doing—where these same kinds of symptoms caused a problem?

Yeah, I mean… at home it’s more like normal little stuff that turns into a problem. Like I’ll forget to finish something I was doing, or I’ll lose track of what step I’m on.

It happens at work too, actually—like I’ll forget to mark a step on a checklist, or not answer a supervisor’s text because I saw it and then thought I’d reply in a second, and then it’s just gone from my brain. Or I’ll leave my safety glasses in my locker and not realize until I need them. And then people act like I’m being careless or I don’t care, but I really do. I just… miss stuff. A lot.
Have you noticed any ongoing feelings of anxiety, low mood, poor sleep, or use of alcohol/drugs that might be contributing to your trouble focusing and restlessness?

Um… I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed anything like that being the main reason, if that makes sense.

Like, I know people ask about stress and sleep and stuff, and I get why, but I don’t know that I can point to one of those and say, “Yeah, that’s what’s causing it.” It kind of just happens even when I’m trying to do things normally.

And with alcohol or drugs… I don’t know, I don’t really think that’s what this is about. It feels more like my brain just jumps off track. But I might need you to explain what you mean a little more.
